style:
Accent: Nigerian English. Tone: warm, clear and upbeat, at a steady natural pace.

Transcript:

lines.c_intro: In many Nigerian lecture halls, students miss what is taught. The hall is crowded, the voice does not carry, a student is unwell, or learning itself is hard. Klasync is an assistive platform for inclusive and accessible education, built so that no student is left behind.
lines.s1a: The lecturer signs in and loads the class roster. Matric numbers are checked automatically, so attendance is verified against real students, instead of a paper register passed around a crowded hall.
lines.s1b: Next, the audio. The lecturer can use the laptop's own microphone, or connect a dedicated wireless microphone for a big hall, so even the back row can hear clearly.
lines.s1c: One tap starts a live session, with a short join code and a QR code, ready to show on the projector.
lines.s2a: Students join from their phones with that code. No account, and no app to install, just a matric number and a name. And because captions are light text, not video, they still come through for a student on limited data, or a weak network.
lines.s2b: For students with dyslexia or low vision, the screen adapts. Larger text, and a dyslexia-friendly font, so the captions are comfortable to read.
lines.s3: Now the lecture begins. Every word is captioned live, for students who are deaf, hard of hearing, or sitting at the back of the hall.
lines.s4: From their seat, a student can check in to confirm attendance, raise a hand, or send a question. For the shy student, or the one who finds it hard to speak up in a packed hall, this gives them a voice, and the lecturer sees it instantly.
lines.s5: While the lecture runs, a live summary builds up. A student who drifts off for a minute, because of tiredness, or difficulty focusing, can glance down and catch up without losing the thread.
lines.s6a: The lecturer can also check understanding on the spot.
lines.s6b: A quick quiz is written from what was just taught. Students answer on their phones, and the results come in live, so the lecturer knows immediately whether the class understood, or needs a second explanation.
lines.s7: When class ends, attendance is scored automatically, and rolled into course analytics, so lecturers can spot students who are slipping away, and reach out before it is too late.
lines.t1: After class is where it matters most. A student who was sick, stuck in transport, or could not take notes fast enough, signs in to their archive, and finds the whole lecture waiting.
lines.t2: The full transcript is searchable, and synced to the recording, so a student can replay exactly the moment they missed, or simply read at their own pace.
lines.t3: Chapters break a long lecture into short parts, so nobody has to scrub through two hours to find one idea.
lines.t3b: And the summary captures the key points, a quick refresher before a test.
lines.t4: The concept map shows how the ideas connect. It helps visual learners see the big picture, and makes it easier to remember how one idea leads to the next. Tap Tour, and it walks through the concepts one by one.
lines.t5: For the student who finds it hard to remember what was taught, whether from stress, fatigue, or a condition like ADHD, flashcards turn the lecture into short, bite-sized practice they can do anywhere, even between buses.
lines.t6: Then a quiz tests real understanding, with instant feedback and a short explanation for every answer, so mistakes become learning, not discouragement.
lines.t7: And if a question is still on their mind, they can ask the lecture itself. Answers come only from what was said in class, and point to the exact moment, so they can be trusted.
lines.c_out: Klasync. An assistive platform for inclusive and accessible education. Every lecture, for every learner.
